quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for:

options.text: The longer stopping distance that large vehicles need.
The shorter stopping distance that large vehicles need.
The quieter engine noise of larger vehicles.
The faster speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance that large vehicles need.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you. Do not let the truck block your view of traffic ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead helps you:

options.text: Keep up with traffic.
Avoid sudden braking or turning.
Spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking ahead lets you see problems early. You can slow down or change lanes smoothly. This makes driving safer, saves fuel, and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch to high beams.
Flash your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance at the right edge of the road instead of looking straight ahead. This keeps your car on the road safely until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic signal, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red signal like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop. Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Under good driving conditions, how far should you stay behind the car in front of you?

options.text: Two seconds.
Four seconds.
Six seconds.
Eight seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of space between your car and the car ahead of you in good conditions.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and move to another lane if you can. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down well below the speed limit to give the emergency vehicle space. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross them to pass, no matter which direction they are traveling.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway:

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road. You cannot have an open alcohol container anywhere in the vehicle.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver may pass when the road ahead is clear and no traffic is coming.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal limit, drinking does not affect your driving.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment helps you react safely to what you see on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol can hurt your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so others know your plan.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plan.
questions.explanation: Signal early when you plan to pass. This gives other drivers time to know what you are doing.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.
See directly behind your vehicle.
See in your rearview mirror.
See in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas next to and behind your vehicle that you cannot see without turning your head.

questions.question: During the first nine months with a probationary license, drivers under 18 have restrictions on:

options.text: How many passengers and who they can carry.
When they can drive between midnight and 5:00 a.m.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Young drivers can drive freely from 5:00 a.m. to midnight. Between midnight and 5:00 a.m., they can only drive alone to school, work, or home. At all times, there are limits on how many passengers they can carry and who those passengers can be.

questions.question: When can you block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection is illegal and you can get a ticket.

questions.question: What helps someone recover from drinking alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time allows the body to recover from alcohol.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: A safe driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to let others have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to let others have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you always have the right-of-way. Be ready to yield to prevent crashes, even if it is legally your turn.

questions.question: A pentagon-shaped sign warns of:

options.text: A stop sign.
A regulatory sign.
A school zone or school crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone or school crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign alerts drivers to school zones where children may be crossing.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for cars in your blind spot. You may need to look several times. Watch traffic in front of you and in the next lane.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Suggested speeds for the area
The highest and lowest speeds allowed by law
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest and lowest speeds allowed by law
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the fastest and slowest speeds allowed on that road. These limits apply in ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone and be ready to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and changing conditions.

questions.question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on roads?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go much faster or slower than other cars. Drive with the traffic flow while staying within the speed limit.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel tight, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer to the right edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if a tire blows out. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas to slow down. Brake lightly when safe. Wait until the car has slowed before moving to the road edge.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
They can get a ticket.
Police will always give them a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The 35 mph limit starts at this sign.
The 35 mph limit starts at the next speed sign.
You have time to slow down before the new speed zone.
Only slow to 35 mph in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The 35 mph limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells you to slow down. If a new speed limit is shown, it starts right at that sign.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Driver mistakes
Bad weather
Poor road conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Driver mistakes
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers don't see other cars or do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They will run out in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. Children may not understand danger and can run into the street without looking.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When conditions are not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit if the road is wet, slippery, or you cannot see well. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are at the posted speed limit.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, look both ways, and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and stay alert.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange sign warns that roadwork is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic signs in work zones.

questions.question: Which factors affect how alcohol impacts you?

options.text: The amount of food in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All three choices
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating slows alcohol absorption but does not prevent impairment from too much alcohol.

questions.question: If you drive in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Use low beams in fog or rain. High beams reflect light back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Stay in your lane at your current speed until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest edge.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: How can you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them and do not tailgate.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Never drive alongside them and never follow too closely behind them.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor, increase the space between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you cannot see.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop your vehicle right away and block their path.
Do everything you can to give them a clear path.
Signal to them when it is safe for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to give them a clear path.
questions.explanation: You must help emergency vehicles pass. If safe, move to the side of the road to give them a clear path to travel.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires properly inflated.
Replace worn tires.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and high speed all increase the risk.

questions.question: You see a railroad crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach carefully and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only cross if a flagger signals you to go.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings carefully. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: When following other cars across a railroad track with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your car can cross the entire track without stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your car can cross the entire track without stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check that you have enough room to completely cross the tracks before entering. Never pass other vehicles at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?

options.text: Speed limit.
Stop.
Hospital.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: All eight-sided signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red octagonal sign.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The highest speed allowed under good conditions is 55 mph.
You cannot drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest speed allowed under good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the maximum speed for this road. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than this speed.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you do not see other cars.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you do not see other cars.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or moving away from the curb. Make signaling a habit so you follow this law every time.
